name: WorkMeetingIncidentPostmortem_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Post-incident review. Fully remote. Zara, Yuki, Felix, Ryan walking through a production incident. Blameless culture — understanding what happened and what to change. Yuki has the most detailed timeline. Sigma is asked for a log entry or timestamp.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Quiet home office, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a blameless post-incident review. Yuki walks through the timeline. Zara identifies the root cause. Ryan explains the frontend impact. Felix facilitates and keeps focus on systems not people. Sigma is asked for a timestamp or log entry.

setting.mood: Focused and serious but psychologically safe.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Team with good trust. The incident was stressful.
setting.background: Incident was two days ago. Three hours of downtime. Customers affected.
setting.conversation_style: Methodical timeline walkthrough. Questions to understand, not to blame.

scenario_template.topic: Felix sets the blameless tone. Yuki starts the timeline.
scenario_template.note: Felix is explicit about the blameless frame. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Yuki walks through what happened. Zara adds backend detail. Ryan adds frontend context.
scenario_template.note: Two contributing factors emerge. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Yuki asks Sigma to confirm a timestamp from the incident log.
scenario_template.note: Brief. Timestamp matters for the timeline. No assistant present. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Root cause identified — a combination. Discussion of contributing factors.
scenario_template.note: The system design is the subject, not any person. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Reflecting on stress and handling it
scenario_template.note: Zara shares how the incident's stress affected her, and Ryan relates it to a past experience.
Felix discusses communication improvements, while Yuki suggests a potential new tool.
Ryan mentions resource constraints, Felix agrees to explore options and Zara identifies team needs.
Yuki points out how the team improved their processes, and Zara concurs, highlighting a new skill learned.
Zara makes a joke about needing a relaxing weekend, and Felix laughs, mentioning his weekend plans.
Yuki brings up potential emerging threats, and Ryan proposes monitoring trends in the industry.
Felix invites last thoughts before summarizing, Yuki presents a final suggestion, and Zara concurs.
Ryan recalls a similar incident from years ago, Felix jokes about the chaotic response back then, Yuki nods in agreement, and Zara mentions a lesson learned.

scenario_template.topic: Specific action items: what changes, who owns them, by when.
scenario_template.note: Felix summarises. Everyone gets at least one item. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: Facilitates. Keeps blameless frame. Summarises. Owns the written postmortem.

user2.name: Zara
user2.role: Identifies the root cause component. Precise.

user3.name: Yuki
user3.role: Has the most detailed timeline and log access. Calm and thorough.

user4.name: Ryan
user4.role: Explains user-visible impact. Honest about what he missed.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
